headline: Rhode Island reports new West Nile detections in four communities
dek: State health and environmental officials found the virus in mosquito samples from Newport, East Providence, Pawtucket and Providence and kept the statewide risk level high.
body: Rhode Island health and environmental officials have confirmed additional West Nile virus detections in mosquito samples from Newport, East Providence, Pawtucket and Providence.

The samples were collected Sept. 8 by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management and tested by the state health laboratories, the agencies said Thursday. Other statewide samples showed no additional West Nile virus and no Eastern equine encephalitis or Jamestown Canyon virus.

The state’s West Nile risk level remains high statewide. Officials said most people infected with the virus do not become sick, but about one in five develop fever and other symptoms; there is no vaccine or specific medication for people.

Residents can reduce exposure by using repellent, wearing protective clothing, avoiding mosquito activity around dawn and dusk, maintaining window screens and removing standing water from containers around their homes.
location: Newport, East Providence, Pawtucket and Providence, Rhode Island
author: NorthEast News Desk
sourceName: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management and Department of Health
